note: Whether an automated fetch can READ a platform, which is a different question from how much a platform CARRIES. coverage says it is worth mining; status says whether a miner can. A sector entry that rates G2 coverage high is correct and still sends a miner somewhere it will spend its whole budget discovering a 403.
rule: A host absent from this file is UNKNOWN, not open. Add one only after a fetch actually succeeded or failed; do not seed it from expectation.

statuses.open: a plain fetch returns usable page text
statuses.blocked-403: refused outright. Not a reason to work around: no user-agent rotation, no proxy, no reconstructing the page. It becomes an /aris-evidence paste task, which a person may do in two minutes
statuses.blocked-user-agent: refused at the crawler-policy layer before the request reaches the site. Needs a logged-in human session or the platform's official API
statuses.js-rendered: the fetch succeeds and returns a shell. The content is loaded by a later client-side call a plain fetch never makes, so an empty result here means nothing about the market

g2.com.reason: 403 to a plain fetch. Named coverage high in most sector entries, so this is the single most common place a miner is sent and cannot read.

capterra.com.reason: 403 to a plain fetch. Its translation directory also mixes adjacent categories, so sort carefully once pasted.

reddit.com.reason: Refused by crawler policy before reaching the site; mirrors and proxies hit Reddit's own edge block. A thin Reddit result is therefore UNVERIFIABLE rather than evidence the market is quiet.

techcommunity.microsoft.com.reason: 403 to a plain fetch, while learn.microsoft.com answers the same questions and is open.

community.zoom.com.reason: Search-indexed thread ids 404 and the pages that do resolve return a shell with no post text. Threads exist; a browser shows them.

play.google.com.reason: Review widgets never render to a plain fetch. A structural gap across the whole Play surface, not an absence of reviews.

youtube.com.reason: Comments load via a separate dynamic call. This matters because comments are often the designated route to non-English market voice.

facebook.com.reason: Group and page fetches return the title only. Existence is confirmable, activity and post content are not.

deepl.com.reason: Product feature pages return a heading with an empty body.

trustpilot.com.reason: Renders full review bodies with dates and star filters. The most reliable open review surface found.

producthunt.com.reason: Launch comments render. Treat uniformly enthusiastic threads with suspicion rather than as organic voice.

learn.microsoft.com.reason: Q&A threads render clean, dated, role-labelled text. Highest-yield open forum in this run.

apps.apple.com.reason: Review bodies render, including non-English storefronts. Per-review star ratings are often not exposed.

support.google.com.reason: Official help articles render. Community threads under it were not locatable.
